beats.beat: The company processes and sells specialty chemicals in four categories: Functional Additives (FA), Chemically Modified Minerals (CMM), Soft Minerals (SM), and Hard Minerals (HM). These are used across industries as additives or modifiers.

The business model is to process raw minerals into value-added chemicals and sell them. The company has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, which provides marketing and distribution support.
The company's top 10 customers accounted for around 59% of revenue from operations in each of FY15, FY16, and FY17, indicating moderate customer concentration.
Exports are made to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka, but the filing does not disclose the export revenue share.

The company lists six competitive strengths: a diversified product portfolio, presence in diversified user industries, import substitution potential, support from its holding company, product innovation through R&D, and a strong management team.

beats.beat: The restated financials cover six periods: six months ended September 30, 2017, and full fiscal years ended March 31, 2013 through 2017. All figures in lakhs of rupees.

Profit after tax turned around from losses in FY13 (–27.40 lakh) and FY14 (–12.17 lakh) to profits in FY15 (149.58 lakh), FY16 (90.18 lakh), FY17 (174.82 lakh), and the six-month period ended Sep 2017 (132.75 lakh).

Cash flow from operations has been volatile: positive in FY13 (200.97 lakh), FY15 (422.36 lakh), FY16 (802.59 lakh), and the six-month period (124.86 lakh), but negative in FY14 (127.73 lakh? actually positive—check: FY14 127.73, but FY17 –349.75 lakh). The FY17 figure was a large negative outflow of –349.75 lakh.
Total assets grew from Rs 2,679.38 lakh in FY14 to Rs 3,424.96 lakh as of September 2017, indicating expansion.
Basic earnings per share (EPS) improved from –0.45 in FY13 to 2.47 in FY15 and 2.43 in FY17; the six-month period EPS was 1.48.
Contingent liabilities aggregated Rs 29.11 lakh as of September 30, 2017, as per notes to the restated financials.
Revenue figures (top line) for each period were not present in the extracted excerpts; the financial narrative is therefore based on profitability and cash flow metrics only.

beats.beat: Promoters are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited (the corporate promoter). Together they hold 89,48,270 equity shares, which is 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up capital. The remaining 0.24% is held by other promoter group members.

The company has entered into related-party transactions in the past five financial years and the six-month period ended September 30, 2017, as per Accounting Standard 18. Details are in the financial statements (page 223 of the DRHP).

Governance concerns include: (i) past instances of non-filing or delayed filing of statutory forms with the Registrar of Companies (ROC), (ii) not yet obtained certain statutory licenses for its manufacturing facility at Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia, and (iii) does not own the premises of two manufacturing facilities and two administrative offices.

beats.beat: The Indian chemicals industry (excluding pharma and fertilisers) was estimated at Rs 5,800–6,200 billion in FY2017. Specialty chemicals (other than agrochemicals and dyestuff) accounted for about 17% of that, or roughly Rs 1,000 billion.

The specialty chemicals segment grew at 10–12% CAGR from FY2014 to FY2017 and is forecast by CRISIL to grow at 12–14% CAGR going forward. Several sub-segments relevant to the company – polymer additives, construction chemicals, water chemicals, personal care ingredients – are expected to grow at 10–15% CAGR.

Key demand drivers include increased consumption, rising GDP, urbanisation, government initiatives like the Draft National Chemical Policy, and 100% FDI in the sector. China's stricter environmental regulations have also created opportunities for Indian specialty chemical makers.
The industry is highly fragmented, with small and medium enterprises (SMEs) holding a 70–75% market share. Only a few Indian players have the scale to compete with global giants.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals is a specialty chemicals processor and seller, offering products like Functional Additives and Chemically Modified Minerals. It relies on a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products.

The company is raising capital through a fresh-equity IPO on the NSE SME platform (NSE EMERGE) to fund a new manufacturing facility in Waghodia, Gujarat, and for general corporate purposes. The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited.
This is an SME IPO, meaning the company is smaller than main-board listings and subject to different eligibility rules, though the disclosure requirements are similar.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of equity shares; there is no offer for sale (OFS) component. The exact number of shares and price band are not disclosed in the DRHP excerpts.

The proceeds will be used to: (i) fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat; (ii) general corporate purposes; and (iii) achieve the benefits of listing on the NSE SME platform (NSE EMERGE).
The lead manager to the issue is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

As of September 30, 2017, the company had an authorised share capital of Rs 2,000 lakh (20,00,00,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each) and an issued, subscribed, and paid-up capital of Rs 897 lakh (89,70,000 equity shares of Rs 10 each).

beats.beat: No long-term agreements with customers or raw material suppliers. The company relies on purchase orders, which means volume and pricing are not assured.
Negative cash flow from operations in FY17 (–349.75 lakh) and volatile cash flows in other years. Sustained negative cash flow could impact working capital and growth.

Not yet obtained certain statutory and regulatory licenses required to operate its manufacturing facility at Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara. Non-compliance could lead to penalties or operational disruptions.
The company, its promoters, group company, and directors are parties to legal proceedings. Adverse outcomes could materially affect financial condition.
Intense competition from domestic and global players, with the industry being highly fragmented. Pricing pressure could reduce margins.
